Windows covering every tick at arbitrarily large depths imply LInfinity. Ext: post-loss cascade, white return, period-four miss and five-step local barrier.

name: Rule30RecurrentStrip
proved: Every finite prefix of a pointed recurrent strip has a power of two as its least common period (`dyadic_prefix_clock`). For any three consecutive ticks, at least one fixed tick has closed runs at arbitrarily large depths (`one_of_three_unbounded`).

name: Rule30RootedWhiteReturns
proved: On a black-edged strip satisfying the left-edge recurrence, for p > 0 at most 2^p distinct p-periodic wheels immediately precede a permanently white wheel. Some wheel at depth ≤ 4^p + 1 fails that clock. On a pointed recurrent strip a prefix clock held through m ≥ 1 is first lost just after a permanently white wheel, where the next wheel flips after p ticks. Arbitrarily deep white wheels have a permanently black wheel two positions further in.

name: Rule30ThreePhaseReturn
proved: A three-tick finite automaton tracking open run lengths modulo three forces a closed run. A reset-free path starting at a white wheel followed by a black one cannot pass a later white wheel and three more wheels (`three_phase_return`). Supplies the finite step for unbounded resets in one of three ticks.

name: Rule30EdgeSourcePulse
proved: For D ≤ k, depth-0 through D right-edge sources contribute one at 2^(k+2)−1 and zero on the next 2^(k+1)−1 ticks (`strip_pulse`). Equal centre readings at the pulse and inside that interval force different deeper-source parities (`deep_must_differ`).

name: Rule30WallRecordAncestry
proved: For every finite wall record of length H and every k, some finite row has that record, a complete finite predecessor tree of height k and no finite (k+1)-step predecessor (`exact_height_with_record`); a one-cell outer edit removes all finite parents (`opposite_ancestry`). Ext: an all-white finite past of a width-W origin is shorter than W. The white-record width H + 2k + 1 and white-past cutoff k = W − 1 are attained.

name: Rule30ResetSwap
proved: Swapping first six- and ten-tick wall returns, given 24 more legal returns, keeps finite width and all rows from tick 11 (`finite_initial_swap`). A trace matching a width-W one below tick W, differing later and rejoining its row, has infinite support (`late_edit_infinite`). The toggle changes exactly ticks 6 and 10. The wall history and final positive half determine its positive past; finite rows that meet preserve the exact outer edge.

name: Rule30DrivenLeftWindows
proved: For driver period P > 0, a start whose leftmost black cell is at -m (m > 0), and onset T, a period-P agreement window of length N in driven column -1 has N + 1 ≤ T + P + m, so a disagreement occurs before 2 * T + P + m (`column_neg_one_period_window_bound`, `exists_period_disagreement_before`). Ext: local versions; depth-sharpened column-pair bounds.

name: Rule30LocalFactor
proved: For every width n, codomain Y, observable g : Word n → Y and update H : Y → Y, if g (step z) = H (g (middle z)) on every block of length n + 2, then g is constant (`autonomous_is_constant`). Uses only left permutivity; the universal-block premise is essential. Ext: Word (n + 2) ≃ Word n × Word 2; fixed-point necessity.

Left edges agree; no eventual period excluded. Ext: all-time agreement on columns p ≤ 1, sharp at p = 2; same for tail_011 splices.

name: Rule30ClockMask
open: arbitrary-prefix propagation; finite-tail period nonloss (stated as remaining open; no Prop named)
proved: Local clock onset cannot be hidden by shorter-period head OR: given even half-clock H, a colour-reversing column, its next two H-periodic neighbours and an explicit 2H clock on the preceding column, the OR and one more predecessor cannot have period H (`OR_not_half_period`, `predecessor_not_half_period`). Ext: triangular-orbit specializations.

name: Rule30RecognizableBarrier
open: Q01 and period 2 (not decided here)
proved: No well-founded rank of width and finite-monoid row image (edge- or wall-read, optionally windowed) falls at every surviving double step of every finitely supported row (`no_recognizable_ranking`); same per centre flip in coupled JointCert frame (`no_joint_recognizable_ranking`); nor integer rank in [-1,width]. Ext: wall-automaton and shifted width-bounded (slack 2) barriers; sharp rows 1493, 1507 coalesce from tick 2.

name: Rule30FiniteClockCertificate
proved: Generic soundness of finite temporal-profile pools: checked left-extension closure covers every finite spatial width (`covers_finite_family`); a checked detection condition propagates a head clock to every column (`finite_family_clock_detected`). Arbitrary transient removal. No arbitrary-clock induction or centre-period exclusion. Ext: multi-period shift invariance of pat; XOR-linearity of accum.

name: Rule30FiniteClockSixteen
proved: A checked 68-node certificate proves any eventual head period of a finite triangular orbit whose full clock divides sixteen is a period of the whole state (`eventual_period_detected`, `period_loss_requires_infinite_tail`); width and transient unbounded. No centre-column period excluded. Ext: eventual head period H ⇔ full-state return iterate x H = x ⇔ all-column period H.

name: Rule30TerminalClock
open: completeness of the rewrites; arbitrary head-clock detection (stated as remaining open; no Prop named)
proved: The known terminal response rewrites preserve every equality between full triangular orbit states, behind every shared finite prefix and at all times; hence every full-state return time, with no temporal-clock bound (`iterate_equal_iff`, `rewrite_return_iff`). Ext: RewriteEq closed under iterate; 4-bit return preservation 0101↔01, 1011↔11.

name: Rule30CenterRuns
proved: Centre-column block of L equal cells starting at time a≥1: L≤a if black (`black_run_le`), L≤a-1 if white, L≤a-3 for white with a≥3 (`white_run_le_three`). Hence both colours in every window [a,2a]; log2 n ≤ blackCount n; m white cells before 4^m. Ext: blackCount + whiteCount = n; two-sided logarithmic bounds; FinConfig black-run bound.

name: Rule30ResetFreeCore
proved: Sound dead/transient-rank certificates and a kernel-checked 7776-state presentation for five rows avoiding words 0 1^(3m+1) 0; every infinite encoded path has five-periodic first-row output from column seven (`encoded_path_five_from_seven`). Ext: iterate semigroup law; 5k output invariance from index 7; period-15 return on coreStates.

name: Rule30ResetFreeRuns
proved: Every ordinary one-sided row avoiding 0 1^(3m+1) 0 admits a faithful run-length-modulo-three colouring after a finite prefix, including constant-one tails (`exists_coloring`); no colouring premise is left to assume. Ext: shift invariance of AvoidReset; constant rows satisfy it; ColoredFrom unique after any zero.

name: Rule30ResetFreeStrip
proved: If five consecutive literal Rule 30 rows have tails avoiding 0 1^(3m+1) 0, the first row has an eventually five-periodic spatial tail (`five_reset_free_tails`); base-six encoding and transitions proved symbolically; colouring and encoding premises discharged. Ext: shift equivalence for EventuallyAvoidReset; multi-period p + 5m strip periodicity.

name: Rule30ResetFreeBoundary
proved: The five-row tail theorem on actual zero-wall evolution at any time: unless the current spatial tail is already five-periodic, one of the next five rows contains reset words arbitrarily far out (`arbitrarily_far_resets_in_five`). Finite zero tails are five-periodic; no finite-predecessor or Prize claim. Ext: zrow L T (p + 5k) = zrow L T p.

name: Rule30ResetFreeThree
proved: Every nonzero finitely supported zero-wall row contains a word 0 1^(3m+1) 0 at time zero, one or two (`finite_nonzero_reset_in_three`), by a checked 20-state reachable set; two rows do not suffice (`sharpness_two_rows`). No finite-inverse closure, odd-black extinction or Prize statement. Ext: three-row reset-free FinSupp start ⇔ zero; pairAt 1 forced reset at t = 2.

name: Rule30EtherThreeErosion
open: Q001, C3s001, C3w(011) stay open (no walls involved); AbsorptionT t001 is false; absorption3_excludes is vacuous
proved: Period-3 (12×3) ether erodes: column 0 ether-driven, columns 1..k and beyond k+w on the ether, some column off it ⇒ a column in 1..k leaves within 3w+6 steps (`erosion3_fin`). No wall of any width (`no_wall`); ether-and-wall route to least period 3 closed. Ext: uniqueness of Front and REdge; (12,3) spatio-temporal periodicity of eth.

name: Rule30WhiteTailErosion
proved: If column zero is driven by the period-three ether and the right half is white beyond W at time T, every prefix 1..k departs from the matching ether by T+3*max(W+12-k,0)+6 (`white_tail_erosion`); column one departs arbitrarily late. No centre-period exclusion. Ext: column 1 departs from the ether arbitrarily late for every finitely supported right half.

name: Rule30XorRigidity
proved: For any two ordinary Rule 30 histories on all integer sites, their pointwise XOR follows Rule 30 iff one history is zero or both are identical (`xor_history_iff`); no support or periodicity assumption; a nonzero history has exactly two XOR partners (`standard_two_partners`). Ext: F_2 vector-space laws of add; add A B = zero ⇔ A = B; evol XOR rigidity.

name: Rule30StripeMeeting, Rule30Certificates.StripeMeeting
open: completeness for equal infinite traces; numerical-normalizer equivalence; Problem 1 (all stated as remaining open)
proved: For finite integer rows and every centre index, a common stripe-prefix cut with white separator preserves the entire centre trace (`stripe_related_same_trace`); rows becoming stripe-related at any finite time with agreeing prior centre observations were related at time zero or one (`no_delayed_stripe_meeting`). Ext: even-step all-time persistence of StripeRelated; unconditional joint trace/stripe equivalence.

name: Rule30PaddedWords
proved: One bound for every tail of a zero-padded repeating word (`no_padded_word`, `no_padded_word_black`): 7 for 1111; 8 for 11; 9 for 1, 1011, 10011, 10111, 11011, 101111; 11 for 1101; 17 other pure-black tails of length ≥3; 49/69/74 other tails of ≤4/5/6 cells; longer via paddingThreshold. Ext: 7 ≤ paddedBound u; two-sided split and post-padded exclusions.

name: Rule30ParametricStripCertificates
proved: Parametric strip certificates with semigroup saturation exclude repeating words 1^r u for all r ≥ r0 (`not_eventually_param_word`), for all configurations with a leftmost black cell: r≥9 for u = 0, 00, 000, 0000, 0100, 0010, 0110 (was 18 or 27), r≥8 for 010; six length-5 blocks. Ext: two-sided split a^r1 u a^r2 (r0 ≤ r1+r2) and post-padded u a^r exclusions.

name: Rule30CoupledEmptyRight
open: coupled question (CQ) for these words: only the R-empty case is settled here
proved: With empty right half (R empty), no coupling in any phase for period-4 words 0001, 0011, 0111 and period-3 word 001 (`no_empty_right_coupled_0001`, `no_empty_right_coupled_001`); finite survival under bounded left-cone support; speed-1 left-permutive difference-front propagation. Ext: unconditional all-black CQ; complete strict period-4 empty-right exclusion; finite-time centre divergence bounds.

name: Rule30FrozenRuler
proved: Row whose right-edge code agrees with single cell's orbit below bit k≥2 but not k+1 stays so forever at a fixed phase; white run behind edge is single cell's capped at k-1 (`frozen_ruler`); single cell never emits width k-1. Ext: uniqueness of the frozen-ruler depth k; equivalence and monotonicity laws of AgreeBelow.

name: Rule30EtherCutEdge
proved: For every N, the edge code of c7cut N begins 1 0 0 0 0 0 0 1 0 (depth 8, phase 16) and never agrees below bit 9 with the single cell's code, so no row of it translates a single-cell row (`c7cut_not_seed_row`). The seed's flush first thirteen cells never lie in the ether c7; twelve do at time 55 (`seed_no_flush_ether`).

name: Rule30EdgeStaircases
proved: Every alternating stretch of length ≥ 3 whose front is W ≥ 2 cells from the single cell's right edge ends by the first multiple of a period of right diagonal W + 1, within 2 ^ (W + 1) rows (`staircase_ends`). The odd edge codes with T (T c) = c are exactly -1/3 and 1/3 (`period_two_iff`), so rain rows (01)^n alternate for ever (`rain_row_eternal`).

name: Rule30PrefixMerger
proved: Beside the white wall, the starts 1100011 and 1010101 followed by the same arbitrary tail have equal rows from time 2, as do their truncations at every common depth W ≥ 7; depth 7 is needed (`mergePrefix_two`, `mergePrefix_needs_seven`). In Theta, free bit 0 with free bits 1 and 2 black changes only depths 1..6 (`theta_truncate_merge`).

name: Rule30LateTwins
proved: For every nonzero natural y and t ≥ 46, iter F (t - 2) y has a twin of the same width, the same depth-1 cell and the same image two ticks later (`late_twin`). If y never reaches an even value under G and t is even, the twin never does either and lies off y's orbit (`late_twin_immortal`, `late_twin_off_orbit`).

name: Rule30AgeEightInverse
proved: For every nonzero finite row beside the fixed white wall and t ≥ 8, every predecessor of its age-t image is finite, with the exact edge one cell behind (`finite_row_aged_image_all_predecessors_true_edge`). Age 7 is sharp, by a cofinite predecessor. Not a proof of Q01. Ext: classification of 1-step inverses into two branches.

name: Rule30AgeTwentyFourInverse
proved: Every two-step predecessor of a nonzero finite fixed-wall row aged ≥ 24 ticks is finite, with the exact edge two cells behind (`finite_row_aged_image_two_step_predecessor_true_edge`). Age 23 is sharp, by a cofinite two-step ancestor. Not a proof of Q01. Ext: twins from age 25/26; true-edge inheritance for Theta.

name: Rule30PairedColumnRuns
proved: If columns 0 and 1 have period P from time 0 and column 0 is black at some time, every white run of row 0 to their left has length ≤ 2P - 2 (`zero_run_le`), and a black-bounded odd run of length 2m + 1 ≥ 3 needs P ≥ m + 3 (`odd_zero_run_le`). Vacuous when there is a leftmost black cell (Jen).

name: Rule30RightProfiles
proved: For even q, take profiles under the right-diagonal recurrences with d q-periodic, a complementing at q, b 2q-periodic and c complementing at 2q. They satisfy z (t + 4q) = z t xor eta with eta = parity (q/2) xor E_q d (`shift_law`), also on actual diagonals (`rightDiag_shift_law`). The statements are conditional. Ext: unconditional 8q-periodicity on actual right diagonals.

name: Rule30TemporalProfiles
proved: For periodic left-diagonal profiles with C(t+1) = A(t) xor (B(t) or C(t)): a nonzero driver has exactly one periodic child (`child_unique`, `child_exists`), with pulse weight laws (`pulse_source_weight`). An infinite chain of q-periodic child triples starting white has another white profile at an index in 1 … 2^(2q) (`rooted_chain_returns_bounded`). Ext: over all nonzero labelled Q-bit first children, first white gaps sum to at most (2^Q − 1)(2^Q + 1), every Q > 0 (`pooled_first_return_bound`).

name: Rule30RecordCharge
proved: Right diagonal R j has period 2^B(j) with B(j) = ⌈j/2⌉ + Q₀(⌊j/2⌋) = j/2 + O(log* j), where Q₀ comes from the tower T(0) = 1, T(q+1) = T(q) + 2^(T(q)+q) (`Rule30RightPeriods.per_upper_half`). This sharpens the exponent (2j+1)/3 for every j ≥ 18 (`B_lt_two_thirds`, `exponent_bound_before_threshold`).

name: Rule30DifferenceOrder
proved: Defines the order over F₂ of a Boolean stream of period L = 2^e: the largest r whose (L − r)-th finite difference vanishes. Proves its reset and countdown laws (`order_countdown`), using only that the 2^v-th difference is the shift by 2^v plus the identity. Ext: Vanish (2 ^ v) g ↔ g is 2^v-periodic.

name: Rule30UniversalStart
open: Ext: Problem1 ⇔ its period-≥ 2 form (`contextual_distinction_and_problem1_iff_ge_two`)
proved: Take a start with its rightmost black cell at 0, and let m ≥ 2 be the first index with x (-m) = x (-(m - 1)). Then right diagonals D (m+1), …, D (m+6) have least periods 4, 8, 8, 16, 32, 32, and D (m+7) has 32 or 64 (`universal_start`). Every nonzero finite start has such an m (`universal_start_finite`). At matching centres the right temporal difference cancels the centre term. Problem 1 is equivalent to two-sided XOR mirror escape for all P ≥ 2.

name: Rule30RingOrbits
proved: In the frame Phi x i = x i xor (x (i+1) or x (i+2)), m-periodic configurations with orbit x P = x correspond bijectively to closed walks of length m of P-periodic profiles under the right-diagonal recurrence (`encode_walk`, `decode_ring`, `encode_decode`). On rings of positive size, orbit x 2 = x only for white and alternating (`ring_period_two`); only white is fixed.

name: Rule30GateClocks
proved: For any two-input gates g j and any seed, with x_j(t+1) = x_j(t) xor g j (x_(j-1)(t)) (x_(j-2)(t)), every window obeys the record-charge bound (`prefix_window_bound`), so the first n bits have period dividing 2 ^ B n (`prefixExp_le_B`). Affine gates give a period dividing 2 ^ r once n + 1 ≤ 2 ^ r (`affine_prefix_bound`).

name: Rule30White17Runs
proved: For every nonempty list of blocks (r, q) with r ≥ 1 and q ≥ 17, the single-seed center column is not eventually the repeating word 1^(r₁) 0^(q₁) … 1^(rₖ) 0^(qₖ), whatever the transient (`not_eventually_long_white_runs`). So every nonconstant eventual period has a cyclic white run of length ≤ 16.

name: Rule30GrammarRuns
proved: Take any nonempty list of blocks (r, q), each from the categories r = 1, q ≥ 10; r = 2, q ≥ 8; r = 4, q ≥ 7; r ≥ 9, q ≥ 9. The single-seed center column is not eventually the repeating word 1^(r₁) 0^(q₁) … 1^(rₖ) 0^(qₖ), whatever the transient (`not_eventually_grammar`).

name: Rule30TernaryWaves
proved: Every ternary code Int → Fin 3 maps injectively to a row of exact minimal moving return P in the Phi frame, at P = 12 (three 34-cell tiles) and P = 15 (three 31-cell tiles) (`free_ternary_period_twelve`, `free_ternary_period_fifteen`). This gives at least 3^(n / L) words of length n, and physical waves (`ternary_wave_twelve`).

name: Rule30ResetMixtures
proved: For every list of white gaps, all at least 9 and some at least 17, the center column never eventually repeats the concatenation of blocks 1 0^q, whatever the transient. Block count and gap lengths are arbitrary (`not_eventually_reset_mixtures`).

name: Rule30RunEnvelopes
proved: Soundness of strip envelopes at arbitrary width (`covers_sound`), and a criterion excluding periodic words from invariant masks and column observations (`no_word_of_invariant`, `no_black_white_of_envelope`).

name: Rule30RankedWords
proved: For ranked strip envelopes of arbitrary width, rank cannot rise through concatenated blocks (`ranked_append`), and a rank-preserving periodic profile contradicts masked Jen (`no_word_ranked`).

name: Rule30FastImage
proved: A sound bit-parallel checker for strip-image inclusion at every width (`fcovers_sound`, `fimage_mem`), used by the finite family certificates.

name: Rule30LongWhiteSupport
proved: Composition rules for strip masks at arbitrary width: repeated-colour capture, closure and joint capture (`repeat_capture`, `repeat_closed`, `joint_capture`).

name: Rule30WedgeParity
proved: For left-permutive rules a ⊕ g(b, c) with g = γ ⊕ α b ⊕ β c ⊕ κ bc, the zero-wedge count of admissible rows has parity α ⊕ r when κ = 1 (`wedge_parity_quadratic`); when κ = 0 it is α at n = 1 and 0 from n = 2 (`wedge_parity_affine`). Rule 30 with r = ℓ = 0 is odd for every n (`rule30_wedge_odd`), as is Rule 180; this is the parity of OEIS A400898.

name: Rule30FirstChecks
proved: Rows of width ≤ 2 n that are black at column -1 at every even tick through 2 n number 2 ^ n - ones n (`first_check_count`). From check 2 on, at most one of any three consecutive checks is near constant (`two_of_three`); for the others the passing share lies in [1/40, 39/40] (`first_check_balanced`). Covers the first check only; not Q01.

name: Rule30FirstCheckDegree
proved: In the ANF of check n, the coefficient of f 0 ⋯ f (n - 1) is n mod 2 (n ≥ 1), and that of the monomial without f 1 is n + 1 mod 2 (n ≥ 2). So the degree is n for odd n and n - 1 for even n (`check_degree`), and ones n ≡ n mod 2 (`ones_parity`). Ext: the other phase has full degree and is never balanced.

name: Rule30P2Bridge
open: Problem2 ⇔ shellMax o(N) ⇔ F_k → 0 ⇔ orderedEnergy o(N^2) ⇔ maxBlockEnergy o(N^2); Ext: energy forms along progressions ⇒ Problem1 (`problem1_of_subseq_shellMaxLittleO`) and ⇒ Problem1 ∧ Problem2; Problem 2 open
proved: For every Boolean sequence, these are equivalent: half density; shell maximum M_k = o(N) at N = 2^k; flexible energy F_k → 0; ordered energy o(N^2); maximum block energy o(N^2) (`problem2_iff_shellMaxLittleO`, `problem2_iff_maxBlockEnergyLittleO`). Control: the weaker dyadic hypotheses do not give density 1/2 (`weakened_hypotheses_do_not_give_densityHalf`). Ext: energy forms exclude odd periods.

name: Rule30SurvivalBridge
open: repeat budget at length r ⇔ mortality at length r (`budgetAt_iff_mortalAt`, `budget_iff_mortality`); budget at every capacity ⇒ mortality for every capacity function (`mortality_of_capacity_budget`); mortality ⇒ Q01 (converse unknown); none proved
proved: Proves the run bound and the survival inequality for the auxiliary frontier: finite words over {0,1,2,3} read from two adjacent anti-diagonals and updated by the partial scan Z (`runBound`, `survival`). Control: the counting inequality fails for tapes in general (`survival_counting_fails_without_runBound`).

name: Rule30AlternatingTraceBridge
open: mortality ⇒ the center is not eventually period 2 (`center_not_eventually_period_two_of_mortality`); mortality ⇒ Q01 (`Q01_of_mortality`); budget ⇒ Q01 (`Q01_of_budget`); mortality open, converse unknown
proved: A nonzero finite row whose center trace has c(t + 2) = c(t) and c(1) ≠ c(0) from time 0 yields a legal frontier that passes every guard (`immortalFromAlternating`); so does a counterexample to Q01 (`immortalFromHistory`). Control: the 7-periodic row with ones at j ≡ 6 (mod 7) has an alternating center (`alternatingCenter_without_finiteSupport`).

name: Rule30FrontierChart
open: Q01 ⇒ mortality (`mortality_of_Q01`), so Q01 ⇔ mortality (`mortality_iff_Q01`) ⇔ repeat budget at every length (`budget_iff_Q01`); none proved
proved: Read as a space-time chart, an immortal frontier obeys the rule-30 recurrence at every depth ≥ 2 (`Z_rec`, `chart_interior`), with a white wall from time one (`chart_wall`). So its row at time two is a finitely supported zero-boundary start with column -1 black at every even step (`zrow_chart`, `finSupp_start`).

name: Rule30WedgeBridge
open: BWH (open: for n ≥ 7 no stream with a binary prefix of length 2n + 2 has a constant wedge in {2, 3} of length n + 2); RW (open: rotated form with a hard-core junction); BWH ∧ SmallRW ⇒ RW (`bwh_implies_rw`); RW ⇒ BWH (`rw_truncates_to_bwh`); Ext: BWH ⇒ RW unconditionally (`bwh_implies_rw_unconditional`)
proved: Proves the finite-horizon step `maximal_drop_inheritance`. Controls show that the small cases and the hard-core guard cannot be dropped (`small_control_table`, `hard_core_guard_control`). Ext: SmallRW proved (`smallRW`); polynomial-time cone and wedge stepping.

name: Rule30SeparatorBridge
open: RW ⇒ no hard-core e has inverse e eventually constant in {2, 3} (`rw_implies_constant_tail_separator`); RW ⇒ no hard-core e has inverse e = liftWord u (const c) (`rw_implies_orbit_separator`); RW open
proved: A constant separator implies the full orbit separator (`constant_separator_implies_full_orbit_separator`). Control: the hard-core condition is needed (`no_pull_without_hard_core_control`).

proved: Three eventually periodic InX starts: rowA repeats 1011111; rowB is 11 then repeats of 01001011001000; rowC repeats 1100001. Two ticks map A and B to C and C to A (`two_cycle`). A and B differ at every depth 14 q + 3, so InX rows with the same row after one double step need not share any tail (`not_unrestricted_closing`).

name: Rule30SeparatorEquivalences
open: OrbitSeparator ⇔ ConstantTailSeparator; separator ⇒ no zero cut and no finite peel rank for hard-core streams (`separator_excludes_zero_cut`, `separator_excludes_finite_peel_rank`); neither separator proved

Ext: inverse is bijective (`inverse_bijective`); OrbitSeparator holds for label words of length ≤ 3 (`orbitSeparator_length_le_three`).

open: SEP ⇒ no nonconstant period-two center trace on any nonzero finite row (`sep_implies_period_two`); RW ⇒ the same (`rw_implies_period_two`); BWH ∧ SmallRW ⇒ the same (`bwh_small_implies_period_two`); each ⇒ the center is not eventually period 2; Ext: BWH ⇒ OrbitSeparator (`bwh_implies_orbit_separator`); open whether SEP ⇒ Q01, RW ⇒ Q01, or Q01 ⇒ RW/BWH
proved: A coordinate dictionary between the actual diagram and hard-core streams, proved from four local bits (`actual_cone_chart`, `actual_endpoint_hardcore`). Control: the finite origin cannot be omitted (`finite_origin_control`).

name: Rule30SeparatorQ01
open: ConstantTailSeparator ⇔ QN, i.e. Q01 for those free bits (`sep_iff_QN`); Q01 ⇔ SEP ∧ the adjacent-whites case (`Q01_iff_sep_and`); Q01 ⇒ SEP (`Q01_sep`); SEP ⇒ Q01Gap and SEP ⇒ CQ01Empty (`sep_Q01Gap`, `sep_CQ01Empty`); SEP ⇔ LR1 (`sep_iff_LR1`); BWH ⇔ exact-width death bounds (`bwh_iff_deathBounds`); BWH ⇒ Q01 (`bwh_Q01`); none of SEP, BWH, Q01 proved
proved: A chart sends each constrained zero-boundary start to an endpoint stream whose inverse cone is its own run (`cone_chart`, `peel_chart`). The endpoint of Theta f is hard-core iff the free bits f have no two adjacent whites (`hardCore_endOf_iff`). Kernel controls show that neither death-bound guard can be dropped (`odd_guard_needed`, `even_threshold_needed`). Survival forces a unique even bit. At width 33 the seed 6561191253 survives through 31 and fails at 32.

name: Rule30Rule180LoneSeed
proved: Rule 180 (a ⊕ b ⊕ bc) from the lone seed: the support is cell t at even t and cells t - 1, t at odd t (`evolve_seed`), and the center column is 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, … (`center_eq`). So the odd wedge counts it shares with Rule 30 say nothing about the center column. Not about Rule 30.

name: Rule30TopCoefficient
proved: For quadratic left-permutive a ⊕ g(b, c) with g = γ ⊕ α b ⊕ β c ⊕ bc and n = m + 2, the ANF coefficient of x_{-n+2} ⋯ x_n in the center function is 1 ⊕ α ⊕ β for every γ (`top_coefficient_rows`, `top_coefficient_quadratic`). It is 1 for Rule 30 (`rule30_top_coefficient`) and 0 for Rule 180. Concerns rows of width 2n + 1, not the seed.

name: Rule30CenterCylinders
proved: With gap g_t and u = t - g: g_t = g, x t 0 = 0 and x t 1 = 1 iff x u [-g, g + 1] ∈ 1^(2g-1) {010, 011, 100} (`cylinder_iff`). On the single seed every white center time t ≥ 2 has a unique gap, with 2 g_t ≤ t (`gap_exists_of_white`, `gap_unique`). N11 H is a sum of cylinder indicators (`white_black_count`).

name: Rule30BlackTimeGrowth
proved: The center's black times b_0 = 0 < b_1 < … satisfy 5^j (b_j + 20) ≤ 20 · 8^j (`black_time_bound`). So whenever 20 · 8^j ≤ 5^j (N + 19), the first N center cells hold at least j + 1 black ones (`log_eight_fifths_le_blackCount`). This raises the base of the logarithmic bound from 2 to 8/5.

name: Rule30ConeCube
proved: Let d j be the first depth at which the right diagonals stop having period 2^j; then R (d j) (z + 2^j) = ! R (d j) z (`fresh_digit`). For every m and A, the reads u ↦ (cell (u + d j) u)_(j < m) map the 2^m columns A ≤ u < A + 2^m bijectively onto Fin m → Bool (`cube_injective`, `cube_surjective`), with m · 2^(m-1) black cells (`cube_count`).

name: Rule30SourceEnergy
open: TotalEnergySmallO ⇔ SourceEnergySmallO ⇔ OffDiagUpperSmallO ⇒ Problem2 (`sourceEnergySmallO_iff_offDiagUpper_and_problem2`); Problem 2 open
proved: Source energy controls the squared dyadic discrepancy by a van der Corput bound. For n≥2 its diagonal contribution is (2n−1)2^(n−1)+1 (`Ediag_eq_closed_form`), leaving a one-sided upper bound on off-diagonal energy sufficient for Problem 2.

name: Rule30BlackPhaseEscape
open: UBE (open: every finite nonzero left start driven by every periodic word w with a black phase eventually has L w s t (-1) ≠ ! w (t + 1) at some black phase t); UBE ⇒ Problem1 (`problem1_of_UBE`); UBE ⇒ CQ ω for every periodic ω with a black phase (`CQ_of_UBE`); UBE ⇒ Q01 (`Q01_of_UBE`); Ext: UBEAt 2 ⇔ Q01 (`UBEAt_two_iff_Q01`); converses unknown
proved: At a black center time, center (t + 1) = ! cell t (-1), whatever the right half. The all-black word escapes by time m + 1 (`allBlack_escape`). Ext: unconditional escape at period 1 (`UBEAt_one`).

name: Rule30PeriodTwoMass
